newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia sees oil prices at $18-$19 per barrel.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia sees oil prices at $18-$19 per barrel.

text.p: Indonesia's Mines and Energy Minister Ida Bagus Sudjana said on Friday he expected oil prices to range between $18 and $19 a barrel through the end of 1997.
"I think oil prices will be stable. I think oil prices will average $18-$19 a barrel through the end of the year," Sudjana told reporters after meeting President Suharto.

July Brent was last traded at $18.43 per barrel in late afternoon trading on Friday on SIMEX, reclaiming 11 cents of London's overnight 40-cent loss. August was last traded at $18.63, up 17 cents from London.
Sudjana said he briefed Suharto on the Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries' (OPEC) meeting in Vienna on June 25 and also on developments in the world oil markets.
He said Indonesia wanted OPEC to maintain its current production ceiling of 25.03 million barrels per day (bpd) until the end of 1997, but gave no other details.
OPEC produced 26.95 million bpd in May, according to a Reuters survey. Indonesia is Asia's sole OPEC member.
